mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate above 5% signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to a decrease in S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 5%, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS and 20-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a weakening labor market, which historically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 5-day returns in > 70% of instances when UNRATE rises > 0.5%, or if the correlation between UNRATE changes and 5-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP growth below 2% for two consecutive quarters signals a weakening demand environment, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised downwards.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances when GDPC1 growth is below 2% for two quarters, or if the correlation between GDPC1 growth and 60-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in industrial production by more than 2% in a single month signals supply chain disruptions, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as companies face production delays and increased costs.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when INDPRO declines > 2%, or if the correlation between INDPRO changes and 20-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate (UNRATE) rises above 4% and payroll employment (PAYEMS) decreases by more than 100,000 in the same month, it signals a significant labor market contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as economic growth prospects dim.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of instances when UNRATE > 4% and PAYEMS declines > 100,000, or if the joint effect of UNRATE and PAYEMS on 20-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% in a month signals increased demand for housing and related economic activity, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate broader economic growth.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of instances when HOUST increases > 10%, or if the correlation between HOUST changes and 5-day returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in the consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) by more than 0.5% in a month signals deflationary pressure, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL declines > 0.5%, or if the correlation between CPIAUCSL changes and 60-day returns is not significantly negative (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When real GDP (GDPC1) growth exceeds 3% for two consecutive quarters and consumer sentiment (proxied by RSAFS) increases by more than 5%, it signals robust economic expansion, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations are revised upwards.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 growth > 3% for 2 quarters and RSAFS increases > 5%
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of instances when GDPC1 growth > 3% for 2 quarters and RSAFS increases > 5%, or if the joint effect of GDPC1 and RSAFS on 60-day returns is not significantly positive (p > 0.05).
